items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: He plays similar to Joe Thomas, and that's quite neat within itself.

ctx.x: Right, yeah. But when you say Diz and Stan Levy, this is much later. So, you know, it didn't matter who was on the bandstand as long as they could play, but the Dixieland thing was pretty much a closed shop. You had Joe Thomas, Edmund Hall, Walter Page. I followed Walter Page at

the Downtown when he got arthritis in his fingers and couldn't play and then when I left, I gave it to Leonard Gaskin (inaudible), but Eddie was more Waspish in his thinking than you think he -- he had some friends. (sentence inaudible). I don't know how to come out of that.
